metadata.title: High-Performance Computing Core

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for operating shared high-performance computing platforms in a manner that preserves isolation, integrity, and availability across diverse workloads.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: High-performance computing clusters, batch schedulers, shared accelerators, and tightly coupled compute fabrics.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Establishes baseline trust assumptions for shared and scheduler-mediated high-performance computing environments.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: HPC trust assumptions depend on the physical, jurisdictional, and operational hosting environment.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: HPC platforms commonly rely on trusted bare-metal execution substrates.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Shared platform trust, scheduler authority, and resource contention considerations as defined in NIST SP 800-234.

metadata.remarks: High-Performance Computing Core defines the foundational trust properties required to operate shared, performance-oriented compute platforms. This pattern establishes shared-node isolation, scheduler-mediated authority, and resource fairness as platform invariants, without asserting job lifecycle, accelerator, or application-level controls.

components.title: Shared Node Isolation
components.description: Prevents interference between concurrent workloads executing on shared compute nodes.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Privilege escalation through exploitation of shared operating system or node context.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Isolation controls preventing one workload from impacting others on shared nodes.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Logical separation of execution contexts on shared compute nodes.
Information flow control between node-resident workloads.

components.title: Scheduler-Mediated Execution Trust
components.description: Trust boundaries enforced by batch schedulers and job control systems.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of scheduler or job-control privileges to affect other workloads.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Controlled and auditable access to scheduler and execution control planes.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Least privilege enforced for scheduler and control-plane roles.

components.title: Compute Resource Fairness
components.description: Prevents abusive or monopolizing consumption of shared compute resources.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Denial-of-service via exhaustion or monopolization of shared compute resources.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Enforced quotas, limits, and scheduling policies ensuring fair resource use.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Ensure availability through controlled resource allocation.
